scenes.title: What is a durable workflow?
scenes.narration: A durable workflow is a series of steps that can recover after a process stops. It remembers what happened, then continues from a known point.
scenes.caption: Remember progress. Continue safely.

scenes.title: A simple order
scenes.narration: Imagine an order that reserves stock, charges a card, and sends a receipt. Each step has a result worth keeping.
scenes.caption: One order, several steps.

scenes.title: When something fails
scenes.narration: Suppose the payment service times out. The workflow can inspect its recorded state and retry only the work that still needs doing.
scenes.caption: Recorded state guides recovery.

scenes.title: The design tradeoff
scenes.narration: A retry might run a step twice. So the payment operation needs an idempotency key, and the system needs a clear rule for uncertain outcomes.
scenes.caption: Retries need safe operations.

scenes.title: The useful idea
scenes.narration: Durability comes from remembering progress and designing each step for recovery. The workflow is only as reliable as its external effects.
scenes.caption: Design recovery into the steps.
